reason: At AX-XL, A's balance breaks in the middle of the number ('$12,847. / 33') and its search field gets truncated. B keeps the balance on one line and moves search into the nav bar, so the layout is calmer. A's checkmark chips and pill search look like Material, not iOS. Both have chips cut off at AX-XL. B's pink Pending badge and missing date on 'Today' are minor flaws.

A's dark mode flips the hero to a glaring mint slab, and its web-like chip row wraps 'Reports' onto a row by itself. At AX-XL, A truncates the greeting and its FAB covers the income figures. B is calmer: a large title, a hero that adapts to dark mode, and tidy stat tiles. Weaknesses in B: a light-weight title, dead space at the top, and a FAB that covers content.

Both are near-identical Material-flavored layouts (outlined chips, tinted category icons). At AX-XL, B's balance breaks mid-number ('$12,847.' / '33') and its search field truncates, while A keeps the amount whole. B's Uber subtitle orphans 'St', and its unsigned in/out figures and checkmark chips feel less precise. B's content (dated headers, a P2P transfer) is slightly richer, but that doesn't make up for the rest.

A is cleaner and shows the price beside its CTA, but it has no monthly/yearly choice, which is the core of the request. B has a 'Choose your plan' section, but the plan cards are cut off under the sticky footer, its light-mode status bar can't be seen, and no price is shown near the CTA. At AX-XL size, B's footer also covers more of the screen.

The two are nearly identical. Both use a thin, non-native title. Both also break 'notification/s' mid-word and push the icons out of alignment at AX-XL. B is slightly better: sentence-case iOS headers, 'System' instead of 'Auto', no five-swatch accent-color confetti, and more domain-specific copy. B has an odd empty gap above the title, and its email wraps mid-word at AX-XL where A's truncates.

A uses persistent field labels with Forgot password inline, left-aligned copy that stays readable at AX-XL, and a specific product context (Trailmark, routes and maps). B depends on placeholder-only labels, and its centered multi-line text breaks up at AX-XL. B's logo, name and headline stack takes up vertical space, and its two filled CTAs compete for attention. Both have a solid dark mode.

A breaks badly at AX-XL: the title is cut to 'Aero', the price and CTA are clipped ('$139.', 'Add to...'), and its CTA bar is not full-width. B reflows cleanly with a full-width CTA. B also uses native floating nav buttons. B's weak points: blank color swatches, a cramped price/discount/rating row, and an extra yellow 'New season' accent. A is tighter at default sizes.

B is quieter: a flat mark, a left-aligned title, persistent field labels and a realistic prefilled email. A repeats the app name above the headline, uses a gradient icon, and relies on placeholder-only fields. In both, the colored email CTA competes with the black Apple button. At AX-XL both wrap acceptably but shrink the Apple glyph. A also pushes the Google button below the fold.

Both are near-identical card lists, and both break 'notification-s' mid-word at AX-XL. A has the more realistic domain (fieldnote.app) and a calmer, borderless card style, and its title scales. B's 'Settings' title stays fixed at AX-XL, and its card outlines and five-swatch accent row add noise. B does have native uppercase headers and truncates the email cleanly. Neither shows subscription.

Nearly identical layouts. A has a sharper headline ('Say it once. Keep it forever.') and a native-feeling Skip button in the top bar. B has neither and adds dense legal text. In both, the 'Talk, don't type' row is clipped awkwardly behind the bottom bar. At AX-XL both let the hero card dominate the screen, and both shrink the CTA's mic icon to a tiny size.

A is denser and more useful: a clear hero, a linear goal bar, and pace, time and longest run all visible. It reflows cleanly at AX-XL. B has a native large title and toolbar, but its goal ring repeats the chips and wastes space. B's text crowds inside the ring at AX-XL, its stepper chevrons are faint, and it pushes the key run stats below the fold.

Neither shows a usable monthly/yearly selector above the fold. A's plan card is awkwardly clipped under the sticky CTA, and its light-mode status bar is invisible. B adds price disclosure, Terms and Privacy links, and cleaner footer grouping. At AX-XL both footers swallow the screen; B's legal text crowds out the content.

A is calmer: one hero, two quiet stat tiles, a native-style large title, and a dark mode with a properly darkened hero. B adds web-like outlined chips with an orphan 'Reports' row. Its dark-mode hero becomes a glaring mint block, and at AX-XL the greeting truncates. Both have Material-style tab bars and a FAB that covers content.

B looks more designed at default sizes: native nav bar with cart badge, carded hero, thumbnails, layered dark surfaces. But it breaks at AX-XL (title cut to 'Aero', price '$139.', 'Add to…', badge clipped). A reflows well at AX-XL, but its color swatches render empty (invisible in dark mode), the price appears twice, and the size picker is buried under the sticky bar.

Nearly identical systems. B's headline is punchier with a stronger size ramp, it adds a native Skip affordance, and its 'Already have an account? Sign in' footer is conventional. At AX-XL both push the headline off-screen and clip the content peeking above the footer. B truncates the title and metadata, while A wraps them clumsily and misaligns the play button and link. Overall it's a slight edge to B.

B's hero is a cleaner number, delta and thin goal bar, and its supporting metrics (pace, time, longest run) answer real runner questions. Its 2x2 grid reflows to one column at AX-XL. A's hero piles chips, a ring and a caption together. A's ring text crowds at AX-XL, it leaves a lot of empty header space, and it adds little beyond distance. B's hand-rolled header and tiny chevrons cost it on platform fit.
